originalTitle: Ukrainian drone attacks on Black Sea resort and Crimea kill 11, Russia claims
summary: Seven people, including three children, dead after ‘drone debris’ strike beach in seaside town, says Russian taskforce
content: Ukrainian drone attacks on a Black Sea resort and the annexed Crimea peninsula killed 11 people, Russian officials said after blaming Ukraine for another explosion that killed five people in a Moscow restaurant. Seven people, including three children, were killed when “drone debris” struck a beach in the seaside town of Arkhipo-Osipovka, the crisis taskforce for Russia’s southern Krasnodar region said on social media. Social media videos, verified by Reuters and the BBC, showed tourists in the water and on the shore watching on as what appeared to be a drone slammed into a busy beach. Another four people were killed in a Ukrainian strike on the illegally annexed Crimea, the Moscow-installed governor, Sergey Aksyonov, said in a post on Telegram. Both Crimea and the Black Sea coast are popular holiday destinations for Russian tourists during summer. Earlier, Russia blamed Ukraine for a bombing at a restaurant in central Moscow that killed five people, amid growing speculation that a senior Russian military commander was the intended target. The explosion occurred on Saturday evening near the entrance to an upmarket Italian restaurant in one of the city’s seven Stalin-era skyscrapers on Kudrinskaya Square. Russian prosecutors said an unidentified woman carrying an improvised explosive device had attempted to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard. The device detonated moments later, killing five people and injuring 19 others. In a statement on Sunday, Russia’s foreign ministry accused Kyiv of carrying out the attack, saying: “The bloody tentacles of [Volodymyr] Zelenskyy’s terrorist gang have reached the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant in Moscow.” Russian authorities have not identified the intended target or named the victims. However, pro-Kremlin military bloggers and several independent Russian media outlets reported that the attack may have been aimed at Col Gen Alexander Chaiko, the commander of Russia’s aerospace forces, who was reportedly attending a private banquet at the restaurant to celebrate his 55th birthday. Photographs and videos that appeared online shortly after the bombing, purportedly from the private event, showed a stage with the words “Aleksandr 55” displayed in the background. Chaiko is one of Russia’s top military commanders, having led the failed assault on Kyiv in early 2022 before later being promoted to command the Russian air force. The Telegram channel VChK-OGPU, which is known for publishing leaks from within Russia’s security services, reported that Chaiko escaped unharmed. According to the channel, his daughter, Maria, was seriously injured in the blast, while her husband, Daniil Peredriy, was killed. They were outside on the restaurant’s terrace when the explosion occurred. The Russian newspaper Kommersant reported that investigators believed the woman carrying the explosive device may not have known she was transporting a bomb, suggesting it was detonated remotely by another person, killing her. Among the other reported victims was a member of Russia’s elite Federal Protective Service (FSO). Kyiv has not yet commented on the incidents. Both sides have repeatedly said they do not target civilians in the conflict, which is now in its fifth year. In Ukraine, one person was killed and dozens more injured when Russian planes launched a 90-minute bombing blitz on residential districts in the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, the regional chief, Ivan Fedorov, said on Monday. Since the start of the full-scale invasion, Ukraine’s intelligence agencies have targeted dozens of senior Russian military officers and Russia-installed officials, accusing them of involvement in war crimes. Ukrainian intelligence services have previously employed a range of tactics, relying on both willing saboteurs and unwitting civilians to carry out bombings. They have succeeded in killing at least four Russian generals and several other senior military figures, as well as pro-war activists deep inside Russian territory, although some operations have missed their intended targets. In 2022, a car bomb killed Darya Dugina, the daughter of the ultranationalist Russian ideologue Aleksandr Dugin, in an attack widely believed to have been intended for her father.
chineseTitle: 俄罗斯称乌克兰无人机袭击黑海度假胜地和克里米亚造成11人死亡
chineseSummary: 俄罗斯特遣部队称，“无人机碎片”袭击海滨小镇海滩后，造成七人死亡，其中包括三名儿童
chineseContent: 俄罗斯官员在指责乌克兰制造了另一起导致莫斯科一家餐厅造成 5 人死亡的爆炸事件后表示，乌克兰无人机袭击了黑海度假胜地和所吞并的克里米亚半岛，造成 11 人死亡。俄罗斯南部克拉斯诺达尔地区危机工作组在社交媒体上表示，“无人机碎片”袭击了海滨小镇阿尔希波-奥西波夫卡的海滩，造成七人死亡，其中包括三名儿童。经路透社和英国广播公司证实的社交媒体视频显示，水中和岸上的游客正在观看一架无人机撞向繁忙的海滩。莫斯科任命的州长谢尔盖·阿克肖诺夫 (Sergey Aksyonov) 在 Telegram 上发帖称，乌克兰对非法吞并的克里米亚发动袭击，另有四人死亡。克里米亚和黑海沿岸都是俄罗斯游客夏季热门的度假胜地。早些时候，俄罗斯指责乌克兰制造了莫斯科市中心一家餐厅的爆炸事件，造成五人死亡，越来越多的人猜测俄罗斯高级军事指挥官是袭击目标。周六晚上，爆炸发生在库德林斯卡亚广场上该市七座斯大林时代摩天大楼之一的一家高档意大利餐厅入口附近。俄罗斯检察官表示，一名身份不明的女子携带简易爆炸装置试图进入餐厅，但被保安拦住。该装置不久后爆炸，造成 5 人死亡、19 人受伤。俄罗斯外交部在周日的一份声明中指责基辅实施了这次袭击，并表示：“泽伦斯基恐怖团伙的血腥触角已经伸向莫斯科的巴尔齐·罗西意大利餐厅。”俄罗斯当局尚未确定预定目标或受害者姓名。然而，亲克里姆林宫的军事
